name: DPR Construction
legalName: DPR Construction (privately held, employee-owned; reorganized as a C corporation in 2021)
founded: 1990 (Doug Woods, Peter Nosler, Ron Davidowski — 'the D, the P and the R' — with $750,000 of pooled resources)
employees: 13,500+ across the Family of Companies (company, 2026), including ~6,000 self-perform craft workers
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: DPR is the technical builder of the AI era's flagship site — lead contractor on the Crusoe/OpenAI-Oracle Stargate campus in Abilene, TX (8 buildings, ~4M sq ft, 1.2 GW, each 474,000 sq ft building delivered in under a year) and one of three GCs on Meta's $10B Richland Parish campus. A self-performing GC founded in 1990 and employee-owned since inception (broad-based real-equity program, C-corp since 2021), it hit $14.0B of 2025 revenue (ENR #7, up from #8) with a striking $26.1B of new contracts booked — bookings at ~1.9x revenue implying record backlog. ENR survey data puts 57% of 2025 revenue in the data-center category, ~90% CM-at-risk. Its structural differentiators are ~6,000 in-house craft workers ('a builder, not a broker'), prefabrication claimed on >90% of new work, and an integrated Family of Companies spanning structural engineering (GPLA), digital manufacturing (Digital Building Components), bathroom pods (SurePods), electrical (EIG), offshore VDC (vConstruct, Pune), and a venture arm (WND Ventures). Watch items: a June 2026 TIME investigation into worker injuries at Abilene (a $5,674 OSHA citation later withdrawn; a worker death DPR says was unrelated to site conditions; pending negligence litigation), and the active-but-narrowed CalSTRS lawsuit over its West Sacramento HQ expansion. Collection gap: no audited financials, margins, or backlog — standard for private GCs but notable at $14B scale.
ecosystemRole: The self-performing technical builder of the AI buildout: the GC hyperscalers and neoclouds hire when schedule certainty matters most, converting prefabrication, in-house craft labor, and an integrated engineering/manufacturing family into record delivery speed on the largest AI campuses in the country.

productsAndServices.name: Mission Critical / Data Center Construction
productsAndServices.description: Ground-up greenfield for 'traditional compute densities, cloud, neocloud, and AI infrastructure,' plus retrofit/power-and-cooling upgrades and live-environment work via the Special Services Group. In-house mechanical/electrical/controls expertise through commissioning. Company claims: 2,716 mission-critical projects since 1990, 575+ in the last five years, $12.1B of mission-critical work in the last ten years, >1.5 GW of critical load installed since 1997, 96% of recent mission-critical work with repeat customers.
highlights: Stargate Abilene (Crusoe / OpenAI-Oracle): lead builder with prime partners Rosendin and Southland Brandt — each 474,000 sq ft building (four 25 MW data halls = 100 MW IT) delivered in under a year; campus grew 2 → 8 buildings, ~4M sq ft, 1.2 GW; DCD's 2025 North American Data Center Project of the Year

Meta Richland Parish, LA ('Hyperion', $10B): one of three GCs with Turner and Mortenson on Meta's largest-ever data center (~4M sq ft, >5,000 peak workers, completion ~2030); long Meta lineage back to Prineville OR and Luleå Sweden

Named colocation/wholesale roster: CoreSite, CyrusOne, DataBank, Digital Realty, Equinix, Flexential, Global Switch, NTT, QTS, Stream, Vantage — plus NVIDIA, Oracle, and Applied Materials among advanced-tech customers
Sector ranks: #3 data centers (BD+C 2025 Giants; top 5 since 2016), #4 data centers (ENR 2025 Sourcebook)
productsAndServices.positioning: The 'schedule certainty' seller: ENR's Abilene reporting documents 672 prefabricated exterior panels per building installed at 15-20/day (enclosed in under 8 weeks), steel mill-orders designed in 2 weeks, and a 154-day potential delay re-planned down to 28 days. Versus Turner (pure CM at 2x the revenue), DPR self-performs; versus HITT/Holder (purer DC specialists), DPR carries five-market diversification.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Repeat-relationship CM-at-risk and design-build contracts (~90% CM-at-risk per ENR 2026 data)
productsAndServices.roadmap: Abilene energization completing mid-2026; Meta Richland Parish through ~2030; Gorthy-led mission-critical core market organized January 2026 for hyperscale account strategy

productsAndServices.name: Self-Perform Trades
productsAndServices.description: One of DPR's founding differentiators: ~6,000 self-perform craft workers — nearly half the workforce — executing demolition, concrete, drywall/interiors, doors/frames/hardware, firesafing, electrical, waterproofing, and specialty scopes. 'Annually, DPR's self-performed revenue would rank among the larger specialty contractors in the markets we operate in' (company claim).
highlights: At Abilene DPR self-performs concrete, drywall, doors/frames/hardware, struts, and low-voltage electrical while managing 60 subcontractors (30 more under prime partners)
Direct control of schedule-critical trades is the mechanism behind the speed claims — no waiting on a sub's mobilization for the critical path
Craft retention is the strategic point of employee ownership: profit sharing funds non-owner employees' 401(k)s, weighted toward lower salaries; PTO extended to non-union craft
productsAndServices.positioning: 'A builder, not a broker' — the deepest self-perform bench in the top-10 data-center cohort; both a differentiator against pure CMs and a fixed-cost exposure in a downturn
productsAndServices.roadmap: Craft-training pipelines expanding with data-center scale (per Central Region leadership)

productsAndServices.name: Prefabrication & the Family of Companies
productsAndServices.category: Off-site manufacturing and integrated delivery platform
productsAndServices.description: Prefabrication claimed on >90% of new work, with schedule reductions of up to 50% versus field assembly, powered by an integrated Family of Companies: GPLA (structural engineers), Digital Building Components (digital manufacturing of exterior wall panels, load-bearing light-gauge structures, interior partitions direct from Revit models), SurePods (the largest US bathroom-pod manufacturer), EIG Electrical Systems (electrical procurement/prefab/installation incl. renewables and storage), OES Equipment (jobsite supply), vConstruct (Pune, India — scaled VDC, project controls, software, data), and VueOps (facility-operations/digital-twin software).
highlights: Abilene: 672 prefabricated insulated-metal exterior panels per building, buildings enclosed in <8 weeks; prefabricated anchor-bolt template system; reverse-osmosis flushing projected to cut chilled-water flushing use 75%
Family of Companies employees participate in the same ownership and profit-sharing programs as the parent
70 patents; twice a Fast Company Best Workplace for Innovators
productsAndServices.positioning: The most vertically integrated delivery platform among the DC specialists — engineering, manufacturing, and data capacity in-house where peers subcontract or buy
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Family-company services embedded in DPR jobs and sold externally (SurePods serves outside hospitality/healthcare clients)
productsAndServices.roadmap: Digital-fabrication capacity scaling with the mission-critical book

productsAndServices.name: Life Sciences, Healthcare, Higher Ed & Commercial
productsAndServices.description: The four non-tech core markets that made DPR's name in 'complex and technical' construction — anchored by the landmark Genentech Vacaville delivery (450,000 sq ft biotech plant in 16 months, 2005 — then the world's largest cell-culture facility, and CEO George Pfeffer's career-defining project). Advanced manufacturing (semiconductors, clean energy/battery, aerospace) was organized as its own led core market in January 2026 under Annette Allen.
highlights: Advanced-tech customer roster beyond data centers: Applied Materials, Texas Instruments, NXP, STMicroelectronics, SpaceX, Rivian, BAE, Lockheed Martin, Gulfstream
32 offices including Amsterdam, Frankfurt, Zürich, and Seoul; $1.8B+ of active work in greater Philadelphia at the May 2026 office opening
~43% of 2025 revenue still comes from outside the data-center category — the widest diversification below Turner in the DC top tier
productsAndServices.positioning: Cycle insulation the pure DC specialists lack: life-sciences and healthcare capex runs on different clocks than hyperscale AI
productsAndServices.roadmap: Advanced-manufacturing core market build-out under dedicated leadership

productsAndServices.name: WND Ventures & Construction Technology
productsAndServices.description: WND Ventures (named for founders Woods, Nosler, Davidowski) is DPR's innovation and investment arm: 15+ startups backed since 2015 (Dusty Robotics, ConstructivIQ, Rhumbix among them), relaunched in 2026 with an integrated model pairing investment with operational collaboration — project teams, R&D, and venture investing combined. DPR's VDC practice is a industry pioneer (Leadership Team member Atul Khanzode co-authored 'Integrating Project Delivery'); vConstruct provides scaled offshore VDC/data capacity.
highlights: Named a top corporate VC at BuiltWorlds Venture West 2026
VDC toolset in production: 4-D modeling, BIM coordination, digital twins via VueOps
Quarterly Market Conditions Reports position DPR as an industry data voice (Q2 2026: schedule certainty driving owner decisions)
productsAndServices.positioning: Venture investing wired directly into jobsite deployment — startups get DPR projects as proving grounds; DPR gets first access to tools that compound its speed franchise
productsAndServices.roadmap: Integrated invest-and-deploy model announced 2026; Khanzode/Pfeffer sponsorship

recentDevelopments.headline: TIME publishes an investigation into worker injuries at Stargate Abilene, where DPR is lead contractor: three 2025 fracture incidents, 14 emergency calls since December 2024, an October 2025 worker death (DPR: unrelated to site conditions), and a $5,674 OSHA citation for excavator training (later withdrawn via settlement)
recentDevelopments.read: The highest-profile AI construction site in the country now carries a national-media safety narrative. DPR denied systemic issues and declined to share internal safety data — consistent with its no-published-EMR/TRIR posture, but a transparency gap peers can exploit.

recentDevelopments.headline: ENR 2026 Top 400: DPR rises to #7 on $14.0B of 2025 revenue with $26.1B of new contracts booked; ENR data shows 57% of revenue in the data-center category
recentDevelopments.read: Bookings at ~1.9x revenue imply a record backlog entering 2026. The 57% telecom mix — against the company's 31%-of-2024 mission-critical claim — shows how fast the Stargate ramp tilted the book.

recentDevelopments.headline: Opens a Philadelphia-area office (Radnor, PA) with more than $1.8B of active work in the greater Philadelphia region

strategyRead: 1. (High confidence) We assess DPR's competitive core is schedule certainty manufactured through vertical integration: ~6,000 self-perform craft workers plus prefabrication on >90% of new work plus in-house engineering/manufacturing (GPLA, Digital Building Components) let it compress AI-campus schedules in ways pure CMs cannot — documented independently at Abilene (buildings in <1 year, enclosure in <8 weeks, a 154-day delay re-planned to 28). This is the franchise hyperscalers are paying for.

2. (High confidence) We assess the Stargate Abilene program transformed DPR's risk profile along with its revenue: 2025 revenue +30% to $14.0B with $26.1B booked, but the same site now carries a national-media safety narrative (TIME), pending negligence litigation, and an NDA-bound workforce story. Execution and reputation risk are now concentrated in the exact asset that made the year.

3. (Moderate confidence) We assess DPR is the most cycle-insulated of the data-center specialists: 57% telecom mix versus HITT's 82%, with life sciences, healthcare, higher ed, and an organized advanced-manufacturing market (semis, batteries, aerospace) running on different capex clocks. In an AI-capex pause, DPR's book degrades more gracefully than HITT's or Holder's.

4. (Moderate confidence) We assess broad-based employee ownership is a genuine labor-market weapon in the craft-ceiling era: real equity plus profit sharing weighted toward lower-salaried employees directly targets retention of the scarcest resource (craft labor), and the 2021 C-corp conversion doubling the owner count shows management treats it as strategy, not culture decoration. The unquantified counterweight is the recurring buy-back obligation as owners age out (mandatory divestment at 60-65) — an internal capital call that would bite hardest in a downturn.

5. (Moderate confidence) We assess the Meta multi-GC model (Turner, DPR, Mortenson on one campus) caps any single builder's share of the largest programs by design — hyperscalers are deliberately maintaining a bench of substitutable top-tier GCs. DPR's counter is to dominate the neocloud tier (Crusoe/Stargate) where single-lead awards at gigawatt scale are still available.

6. (Low confidence) We assess DPR's implied 2025 data-center revenue at ~$8B (57% of $14.0B, ENR survey data) — far above trailing third-party estimates of $2-3B, reflecting both the Abilene ramp and definitional noise between 'telecom,' 'mission critical,' and 'advanced technology.' Treat sector-revenue precision as indicative.
